title: Object destructuring, defaults, and renaming
hook: Object destructuring unpacks properties into variables in one expression — with defaults for missing keys and renaming when the API field name collides with a reserved word or local convention.

blocks.text: **Object destructuring** syntax `{ a, b: renamed } = obj` reads properties from **ToObject(obj)** and assigns to bindings. **Default values** apply when property is **undefined** (not when null). **Renaming** `{ id: userId }` binds userId from obj.id. **Nested destructuring** pulls deep paths. **Rest in objects** `{ ...rest }` collects remaining own enumerable properties — order matters for rest placement (must be last).

blocks.text: React props, Express req destructuring, and config objects use this daily. Senior bugs: default not applied for **null** from API, destructuring **undefined** env vars, and mutating rest objects thinking they are deep clones. C# has deconstruction for tuples/records; JS object destructuring is **shallow** and works on any object-like value.

blocks.title: Interview trap: default vs null
blocks.body: const { x = 1 } = { x: null } → x is null, not 1. Defaults only for undefined. Use nullish coalescing after destructure if needed.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Destructuring null/undefined without guard. Expecting default for null. Forgetting = {} on optional options param. Rest before other properties — syntax error.

blocks.text: Performance: destructuring is not free — hot loops may keep property access. **eslint prefer-destructuring** vs readability tradeoff. For immutable updates, destructure then spread: `{ ...user, name: 'New' }`. Combine with **structuredClone** when nested mutation risk. In TS, pair destructure with validated schema at boundary.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying default applies to null. Cannot explain = {} on parameter. Not knowing destructuring throws on null source.

interviewTakeaways: Defaults apply when property is undefined, not null.
Rename with { prop: alias }; nested defaults need = {} on intermediate.
Parameter pattern: function f({ a = 1 } = {}) for optional options.
60s: Shorthand unpack keys to variables. Defaults for undefined only. Rest collects remaining keys. C# needs Deconstruct; JS works on any object. Guard null source.
